Tests: - `npm test -- --verbose` executed successfully (exit code 0). - Jest output includes: - `Require Story Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)` in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - `Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)` in tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Multiple helper/edge-case suites tied to Story 003.0, e.g. `Require Story Helpers`, `Require Story IO helpers`, `annotation-checker helper`. - Overall test summary: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 264 passed, 264 total
Core rules implementation: - `src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts`: - Implements ESLint rule `require-story-annotation`. - JSDoc traceability: - `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED` and related auto-fix/error-message requirements. - Uses shared helpers: `buildVisitors`, `DEFAULT_SCOPE`, `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`, `shouldProcessNode`. - `meta`: - `type: "problem"`, `fixable: "code"`, `hasSuggestions: true`. - `schema` defines `scope` and `exportPriority` with enums from DEFAULT_SCOPE/EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - `messages.missingStory` is clear and actionable, mentioning adding an `@story` annotation and giving an example. - `create(context)`: - Reads options `{ scope, exportPriority }` with defaults from `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and "all". - Binds `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)` and passes it into `buildVisitors`.
- `src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts`: - Implements ESLint rule `require-req-annotation`. - JSDoc traceability: - `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req` entries for REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY, REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED. - Uses shared helpers `DEFAULT_SCOPE`, `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`, and `shouldProcessNode` from `require-story-helpers`. - Delegates annotation checking to `checkReqAnnotation` from `src/utils/annotation-checker.ts`. - `meta`: - `type: "problem"`, `fixable: "code"`. - `docs.description` clearly describes behavior. - `schema` mirrors `require-story-annotation` (`scope` & `exportPriority` with the same enums). - `messages.missingReq` uses `{{functionName}}` and gives a concrete remediation example. - `create(context)`: - Normalizes `scope` and `exportPriority` exactly like the story rule. - Builds `shouldCheck(node)` using `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)`. - Defines visitors for: `FunctionDeclaration`, `FunctionExpression` (excluding those whose parent is `MethodDefinition`), `MethodDefinition`, `TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`. - Each visitor calls `runCheck(node)` which invokes `checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false })` when in scope.
Function detection & shared scope (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - Common node set: - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts` exports: - `DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]`. - `require-story-annotation` uses visitors for: - `FunctionDeclaration`, `FunctionExpression`, `MethodDefinition`, `TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`, and `ArrowFunctionExpression`. - However, `options.shouldProcessNode(node)` is always applied before reporting; since `DEFAULT_SCOPE` does NOT include `"ArrowFunctionExpression"`, arrow functions are never in scope by default and therefore not enforced. - `require-req-annotation` uses visitors for exactly: - `FunctionDeclaration`, `FunctionExpression` (non-method), `MethodDefinition`, `TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`. - Configurable scope & export priority: - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts` defines: - `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)`: - Returns false if `node.type` not in `scope`. - Uses `isExportedNode` to detect export ancestry. - Honors `exportPriority` values: "all", "exported", "non-exported". - Both rules call `shouldProcessNode` with the same semantics and same default `scope`/`exportPriority`. - Tests for scope and export priority parity (from tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts): - Valid cases: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE][Story 003.0] FunctionExpression ignored when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration`. - `[REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY][Story 003.0] non-exported function ignored when exportPriority is 'exported'`. - `[REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY][Story 003.0] exported function required when exportPriority is 'exported'`. - `[REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY][Story 003.0] exported function ignored when exportPriority is 'non-exported'`. - `[REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY][Story 003.0] non-exported function required when exportPriority is 'non-exported'`. - Similar tests for methods and function expressions. - Invalid cases: - Exported/non-exported functions and methods appropriately reported based on `exportPriority`. - Tests for story rule scope/export priority (from tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts): - `require-story-annotation with exportPriority option`: - Valid unexported function without @story when `exportPriority: "exported"`. - Invalid exported function missing @story for same config (auto-fix provided). - `require-story-annotation with scope option`: - Valid arrow function ignored when `scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]`. - Invalid function declaration missing annotation in same config.
Arrow functions excluded by default (part of REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION): - `DEFAULT_SCOPE` does not include `"ArrowFunctionExpression"`. - `require-story-visitors.buildArrowFunctionVisitor` checks `options.shouldProcessNode(node)` before reporting; since scope cannot include arrows (schema enum only allows DEFAULT_SCOPE node types), arrows are always out-of-scope by default. - Test in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - `"[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default"` confirms no error is reported for an unannotated arrow function. - `require-req-annotation` has no ArrowFunctionExpression listener, so arrow functions are never checked, matching the spec that arrows are excluded by default.
JSDoc parsing and common strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED): - For @story (require-story-annotation): - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts`: - `jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node)` uses `sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node)` and checks `jsdoc.value.includes("@story")`. - `commentsBeforeHasStory`, `leadingCommentsHasStory` inspect preceding/leading comments for `"@story"`. - `hasStoryAnnotation` combines: - JSDoc detection - commentsBefore - leadingComments - `linesBeforeHasStory` (line-window heuristic) - `parentChainHasStory` (ancestor comments) - `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` (character-window heuristic) - Wrapped in try/catch for robustness. - `reportMissing` and `reportMethod` call `hasStoryAnnotation`; only report when no existing annotation, and include suggestions with example `@story` JSDoc. - For @req (require-req-annotation): - `src/utils/annotation-checker.ts`: - Retrieves JSDoc via `getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node)`. - Collects comments via `getLeadingComments(node)` and `getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node)`. - Combines them and passes to `hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node)`. - If `hasReqAnnotation` is false, `reportMissing(context, node, enableFix)` is called. - `src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts`: - `hasReqAnnotation` implements multi-heuristic detection: - If `context.getSourceCode()` and a `node` are available, it uses: - `linesBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node)` (scan previous `LOOKBACK_LINES` lines for `@req` or `@implements`). - `parentChainHasReq(sourceCode, node)` (ancestor comments and `leadingComments`). - `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node)` (scans preceding `FALLBACK_WINDOW` characters). - Falls back to JSDoc and comments content checks when no source/loc are available. - Treats both `@req` and `@implements` as satisfying requirement coverage. - All helpers guard against malformed source/loc and catch exceptions, returning false rather than throwing. - These strategies parallel each other: both rules rely on `getJSDocComment`, comments before/leading comments, line-window, and text-window heuristics with defensive guards. - Tests (from tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts): - Validate presence and absence of @req for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - Ensure missing annotations cause `missingReq` errors with correct data fields.
Annotation enforcement (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED): - `require-story-annotation`: - Tests (tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts): - Valid: - FunctionDeclaration with JSDoc `@story`. - Function with only `@implements` line (multi-story support) accepted as satisfying story requirement. - Line comment `// @story ...` before function. - FunctionExpression, arrow function (when annotated), class method, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature — all accepted with proper annotations. - Invalid: - Missing @story on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, class method, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature → `missingStory` errors with suggestions and auto-fix outputs are asserted. - `require-req-annotation`: - Tests (tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts): - Valid: - Function with only `@req`. - Function with only `@implements` (satisfies requirement coverage as per multi-story support). - Function with both `@story` and `@req`. - FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, several TS function-expressions, etc., all properly annotated. - Invalid: - Missing @req with or without @story; all in-scope constructs produce `missingReq` errors with data `{ name, functionName }`.
Error location & messages (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience): - `require-story-annotation`: - `reportMissing` & `reportMethod` in `require-story-helpers` compute a function name via `extractName` and choose `nameNode` as: - `node.id` if it is an Identifier; else `node.key` if Identifier; else `node`. - `context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, ... })` ensures ESLint highlights the identifier for named functions/methods, or the nearest sensible node for anonymous constructs. - Message text is explicit: tells the user that the function must have an explicit `@story` annotation and gives an example path. - `require-req-annotation`: - `annotation-checker.reportMissing` uses `getNodeName(node)` (from `require-story-utils`) to derive a readable name. - Same `nameNode` logic (preferring `id` or `key` Identifiers) and populates `data: { name, functionName: name }`. - Error message `missingReq` is actionable: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') ...". - Tests assert that `data` contains correct `name` and `functionName` and that specific cases for methods use the method name in the payload, satisfying precise error location and context.
TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - Implementation: - Both rules rely on parsers that support TS syntax (RuleTester languageOptions in tests set TS parser/options where needed). - `require-story-annotation` visitors include `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature`. - `require-req-annotation` visitors also include `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature`. - `annotation-checker.checkReqAnnotation` is explicitly documented and annotated for TS support and uses TS-specific node shapes in tests. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - `[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS declare function`. - `[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS method signature`. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - Uses `runAnnotationCheckerTests` for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature, both valid and invalid cases. - Additional TS FunctionExpression in variable declarators, including exported ones, validating detection and enforcement for TS-specific shapes.
Error handling & edge cases (Error Handling acceptance): - `require-story-helpers.hasStoryAnnotation` and `reportMissing`/`reportMethod` wrap detection/reporting in try/catch to prevent exceptions from breaking linting. - `reqAnnotationDetection` helpers guard against: - Missing or malformed `sourceCode.lines` and node `loc`. - Missing or malformed `node.range` and missing `getText`. - All advanced heuristics are inside try/catch; on failure, they fall back to simple checks instead of throwing. - Tests: - tests/rules/require-story-helpers-edgecases.test.ts and tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts (seen in Jest output) exercise malformed/missing JSDoc values and non-standard sourceCode shapes, ensuring graceful behavior.
Documentation (Documentation acceptance): - `docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md`: - References this story: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Documents rule purpose, supported node types, options schema (`scope`, `exportPriority`), examples (correct/incorrect), including TS-specific examples. - Explicitly lists supported node types matching REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION. - `docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md`: - References this story: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Explains behavior, supported node types, options, and multiple examples including TS-specific syntax. - Notes that arrow functions are not checked and that `@implements` can satisfy requirement coverage.
Traceability to story and requirements: - All relevant implementation and helper files include JSDoc annotations pointing to: - `docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Requirement IDs such as `REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION`, `REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`, `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`, `REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY`, `REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT`, etc. - Test files for these rules include `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and requirement tags, ensuring bi-directional traceability between spec, implementation, and tests.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and enumerated requirements for Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are implemented and verified by passing tests. The ESLint rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` share the same function-like detection scope (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) with arrow functions excluded by default, offer aligned configurable `scope` and `exportPriority` behavior, support TypeScript and JavaScript, parse JSDoc and surrounding comments using robust shared strategies, and provide clear, actionable error messages anchored at function names. Extensive RuleTester suites and helper tests confirm correct behavior across normal and edge cases, and rule documentation with examples and configuration options is present. Therefore, this story is fully implemented and passes.
